answer: Adaptive rate-limit decay. Each new identity starts with a low action quota that grows only through sustained, verified activity over time. Attacker cost is linear in identities but sublinear in usable capacity: N fresh identities yield only N^0.5 effective throughput, so each marginal fake costs more real time than the last. Like sand piling against a dune, gains erode. An attacker scraping a canyon of accounts hits basalt-hard diminishing returns at scale.
